response: Yes, delayed peripheral facial palsy in stapes surgery can be minimized or prevented by using proper surgical techniques, such as gentle tissue handling, precise identification and preservation of the facial nerve, and avoiding excessive manipulation or compression of the nerve. Additionally, the use of facial nerve monitoring during surgery can help reduce the risk of injury. Post-operative steroid administration may also be considered to reduce inflammation and swelling that could put pressure on the facial nerve. However, even with these precautions, the risk of delayed facial palsy cannot be entirely eliminated due to individual anatomical variations and other factors.
